info.title: atlas
info.summary: Grounded schema catalogue generation for unfamiliar databases.

get.description: Effective configuration. Secrets are reported as present or absent only.

put.description:
Store the connection string and immediately re-probe.

Writing it also sets it in this process's environment, so there is no
restart between saving a credential and finding out whether it works.

Build and encode a Snowflake URL from normal credential fields.

People should never have to know URL-encoding rules for passwords. The
password is accepted as a secret field, encoded by SQLAlchemy, persisted in
the existing engine-side secret store, and never returned by the API.

post.description:
Connect and report what came back.

Runs inline rather than as a job: two queries, and a setup form needs the
answer before the user moves on.
Capture the physical layer for the workspace's bound source.
Run the analysis agent. Minutes per table — always poll the job.
Rebuild output.yaml from the stored snapshot and claims. Fast; inline.

schema.title: Response Compile Output Workspaces  Name  Compile Post

get.description:
Built on read, never served from the stored file.

Output is derived from the snapshot and the claims. Serving a cached copy
means a reviewer approves a claim and the catalogue still shows it as
generated — the two stores disagree and the UI is the one that looks broken.
`compile` still writes output.yaml, but as an export, not a source.

schema.title: Response Get Output Workspaces  Name  Output Get

get.description:
The emitted view — what an agent would actually be given.

Distinct from `/output`, which is the catalogue: every claim with its
evidence, confidence and review state. This is only what survived review,
phrased for something writing SQL. Both the structured form and the
rendered YAML are returned, because the console shows the second and an
agent consumes the first.

schema.title: Response Get Semantic View Workspaces  Name  Semantic View Get
Response Get Questions Workspaces  Name  Questions Get

post.description:
Settle a question, and let the answer count as evidence.

This is the only path that lifts a business claim past the OBSERVED
ceiling. `ClaimPolicy` has always allowed it for a human decision; until
this endpoint existed nothing could produce one, so every semantics claim
in the catalogue sat at 0.65 with no mechanism able to move it.

schema.title: Response Answer Question Workspaces  Name  Questions  Question Id  Answer Post

post.description:
Set a question aside without answering it.

Not the same as answering: nothing is established, no claim moves, and no
evidence is recorded. It only stops the question being asked again — the
column is dead, the distinction does not matter here, or nobody knows.

schema.title: Response Dismiss Question Workspaces  Name  Questions  Question Id  Dismiss Post

get.description:
Claims, highest-impact first: least certain at the top, since a claim
nobody doubts is not worth a reviewer's attention.

schema.title: Response Get Claims Workspaces  Name  Claims Get

post.description:
Record a human verdict, as evidence.

A decision is written to the evidence store and linked to the claim; where
the claim now stands is derived from that record, never stored on it. See
`APPROVAL.md`.

This no longer refuses an ungrounded claim. The 409 it used to raise existed
because `enforce_grounding_rules` forbids `verified` without an executed
check — but a human decision *is* grounding (`Fact.is_grounded` accepts
`ProvenanceKind.HUMAN`), so the condition is not reachable. What the refusal
protected against is preserved instead by keeping the states apart: a claim a
check established reads as `verified`, a claim only a person asserted reads
as `authoritative`, and the emitted view says which.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: How many tables; null means all remaining

tables.title: Tables
tables.description: Specific tables. Overrides limit and ranking.

regenerate.title: Regenerate
regenerate.description: Re-analyze tables that already have claims, discarding their previous claims and evidence rather than merging. Scoped to the tables in this run. Off by default: regeneration resets human verdicts on reworded claims and drops the observations behind them.

ConnectionHealth.title: ConnectionHealth
ConnectionHealth.description:
The result of actually connecting, as distinct from being configured.

`configured` only means the environment variable holds something. A wrong
password, an unreachable host, or a schema that does not exist all leave it
true — so a card reading "credentials found" was claiming more than anyone
had checked.

Consequence.title: Consequence
Consequence.description: What breaks downstream if the claim is wrong.

Endorsement.title: Endorsement
Endorsement.description: Answers: where does this claim stand with a human?

EndorsementFactors.title: EndorsementFactors
EndorsementFactors.description:
Why the state is what it is.

Deliberately not averaged into a score. Trust is continuous because evidence
varies in strength; a named person either backed the claim or did not, and a
weighted mean over "standing" and "corroboration" would be a number nobody
can act on. These qualify the state; they never replace it.

reset_semantics.title: Reset Semantics
reset_semantics.description: Required when refreshing a workspace that already has semantic state.

JobProgress.title: JobProgress
JobProgress.description:
What a running job is doing, in a shape the console can render.

A sentence alone was not enough: the analysis spends minutes per table, so
the reviewer needs to know which table is under way and how much of the run
is left, not just that something is happening.

id.title: Id
id.description:
Stable across runs, so an answer survives re-analysis.

Keyed on what is being asked rather than on when: re-analysing a table
asks the same question again, and a reviewer should not be made to
answer it twice because the wording of the evidence changed.

SourceStatus.title: SourceStatus
SourceStatus.description:
A declared source, whether its variable is populated, and whether anyone
has managed to connect with it.

Never carries the URL: this endpoint is unauthenticated, and the registry
exists precisely so credentials do not travel through it.

Trust.title: Trust
Trust.description: What established the claim, not how important the claim is.

factor_weights.description: The exact policy weights used, so clients never mirror them.

TrustAssessment.title: TrustAssessment
TrustAssessment.description:
Why a claim has its confidence score.

Stored with a claim so API clients do not have to reverse-engineer a number
from prose provenance. `confidence` remains duplicated on `Fact` for
backwards compatibility and queue ordering; model validation keeps the two
equal for newly assessed claims.

TrustBand.title: TrustBand
TrustBand.description: Human interpretation of a score; intentionally broader than a decimal.

TrustFactors.title: TrustFactors
TrustFactors.description: Inspectable inputs to the trust score, each normalized to 0..1.
